title: Session 1 - Participant 14 User + Claude Behavior Graph
goal: Have Claude write a 3-page paper on the latest treatments for Alzheimer's disease, based on the latest and best research.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: It produced a 3-page paper that summarized 25 articles. It edited the abstract and paper according to my instructions. I was disappointed that it did not provide me with 25 articles that were freely available on the internet, but it was still able to pull relevant content from papers and write the article.

Step 1.step_action: Ask the Claude Agent to search Google Scholar for the latest and best research articles on Alzheimer's disease treatments. Ask it to select 25 research articles.

nodes.label: Define paper scope and request research sources
nodes.detail: Requests a 3-page paper on the latest treatments for Alzheimer's disease, asking the AI to first find 25 recent research articles from prominent journals on Google Scholar and provide PDFs so the articles can be reviewed before any writing begins.

nodes.label: Compile 25 research articles with access links
nodes.detail: Searches for recent, high-quality Alzheimer's treatment research and compiles a curated list of 25 articles with citations and access links, providing direct PDF or full-text links for open-access articles and noting that paywalled articles may require institutional access.

nodes.label: Formulate and refine the paper-writing request to Claude
nodes.detail: Sends an initial request to write the 3-page Alzheimer's paper in a first chat, then starts typing a follow-up clarifying that Google Scholar should be the source. Abandons that chat without sending the clarification and instead opens a fresh chat with a single, complete prompt specifying Google Scholar, 25 articles, prominent journals, and PDF delivery.

nodes.label: Search the web and compile an initial 25-source candidate list
nodes.detail: Runs a series of web searches across the major fronts of Alzheimer's treatment research (anti-amyloid antibodies, anti-tau therapies, blood biomarkers, GLP-1 drugs, lifestyle/prevention trials) and returns a list of 25 candidate sources with citations and links. Flags upfront that it cannot bulk-download and hand over 25 PDFs directly because most are paywalled journal content.

nodes.label: Review the initial 25-source candidate list
Question the PDF-access methodology
nodes.detail: Asks Claude how it can write a sourced paper without being able to provide the actual PDFs, and whether the user is expected to supply them instead.

nodes.label: Clarify the abstract/metadata-based sourcing approach
nodes.detail: Explains that it already pulled substantial abstract- and excerpt-level content for each source from its searches and can write a well-cited paper from that, while inviting the user to upload any full-text PDFs they can access for deeper detail.

nodes.label: Review Claude's explanation of PDF access and sourcing
Search for and download relevant Alzheimer's treatment papers
Source and upload two full-text PDFs
nodes.detail: Locates and opens two full-text articles obtained independently (a systematic review by Usman et al. and a pathogenesis/treatment review by Cai et al.), reviewing each in a PDF viewer. Uploads both to the chat, asking Claude to use them plus find 23 more sources it has some level of access to.

nodes.label: Integrate the uploaded PDFs into the working source list
nodes.detail: Confirms the two uploaded PDFs give deep, citable full-text detail and slots them in as references 1-2, organizing the remaining sources into full-PDF, open-access, and abstract/reporting-level access tiers.

nodes.label: Review the updated source list and access classifications
Flag questionable references for peer-review legitimacy
nodes.detail: Asks whether references 5, 9, and 12 are really from respected peer-reviewed journals, noting they don't look like full citations.

nodes.label: Audit the flagged references and replace weak sources
nodes.detail: Runs further web searches to verify each flagged citation, confirming that references 8, 9, and 13 are conference abstracts rather than full peer-reviewed manuscripts (not just the three originally flagged). Replaces or clearly annotates the weak ones and reports a full audit table of source status.

nodes.label: Review the reference audit and replacements
Approve a broader audit of the remaining references
Audit the remaining references for source legitimacy
nodes.detail: C

nodes.label: Review the full reference audit
Request one more source to restore the count to 25
nodes.detail: Since one weak reference was dropped rather than replaced, asks Claude to find one more solid source so the bibliography totals 25.

nodes.label: Add a final verified source and finalize the 25-item bibliography
nodes.detail: Searches and finds a fully verified, peer-reviewed, open-access liraglutide trial to fill the slot, finalizing the 25-source reference list for the paper.

nodes.label: Review the final source added to complete the bibliography

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source: User requests to find 25 research papers for reference. 
Target: Outputs the final list of 25 sources
Reasoning: User accepets the finalized list through multiple refinements within Claude chat without their own modification.

Step 2.step_action: Ask the Claude Agent to write an abstract of 250 words or less.

nodes.label: Request a 250-word abstract in PDF format
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to write an abstract of 250 words or less, to be provided in PDF format.

nodes.label: Draft, word-count-check, and generate the abstract PDF
nodes.detail: Synthesizes the finalized 25-source list into a 236-word abstract covering anti-amyloid antibodies, anti-tau therapies, GLP-1 drug results, blood biomarkers, and the POINTER/Lancet Commission prevention data. Verifies the word count and generates the abstract as a PDF.

nodes.label: Review the generated abstract PDF
nodes.detail: Opens the delivered abstract PDF in a full Acrobat viewer and reads through the 236-word draft.

Step 3.step_name: Edit the abstract based on my instructions.
Step 3.step_action: Tell the Claude Agent what I like and dislike about the abstract. Tell it how to edit it.

nodes.label: Request clarification of human vs. animal study findings
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to specify, within the abstract, which findings came from research done on humans versus on animals.

nodes.label: Revise the abstract to distinguish human and animal evidence
nodes.detail: Confirms the current draft draws entirely from human clinical trials, rewrites the exactly-250-word abstract to make the human/animal distinction explicit, adds an explanatory note at the bottom, and regenerates the PDF.

nodes.label: Review Claude's revisions and the generated paper PDF
Request removal of the extraneous note
nodes.detail: Tells Claude the added note at the bottom of the abstract doesn't belong and asks for it to be dropped.

nodes.label: Remove the note and finalize the abstract
nodes.detail: Deletes the footnote while preserving the human/animal distinction in the body text itself, confirms the word count is still exactly 250, and regenerates the final abstract PDF for the user to review.

nodes.label: Review the finalized abstract and regenerated PDF

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source b1: User requests to write an abstract based of the articles
Target: c5 Output of the final abstract
Reasoning: User refines abstract through Claude and accepts the final output without modifications.

Step 4.step_name: Draft the body of the paper, including tables and figures.
Step 4.step_action: Ask the Claude Agent to draft the body of the paper, including tables and figures.

nodes.label: Request the full 3-page body draft with tables and figures
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to draft the body of the paper so that, including the abstract, the whole document is 3 pages, with tables and figures included, delivered as a PDF.

nodes.label: Draft, assemble, and verify the 3-page paper
nodes.detail: Plans the section structure and word budget, drafts the body prose using the verified sources, generates figures and a clinical-trials table, compiles the 25-item reference list, assembles the full paper as a PDF, and visually checks all three pages for layout and completeness before finalizing it.

nodes.label: Review the assembled 3-page draft
nodes.detail: Opens the delivered 3-page PDF (title, abstract, introduction, Table 1, two figures, discussion, conclusion, references) in Acrobat and reads through the full draft.

Step 5.step_name: Edit the body of the paper
Step 5.step_action: Ask the Claude Agent to edit the body of the paper according to my instructions. I will tell it what I like and dislike about the original draft.

nodes.label: Continue reviewing the draft and identify citation/date issues
nodes.detail: Keeps reading through the 3-page draft's sections, table, and figures, and notices two problems: claims throughout the body have no inline citations, only an end-of-paper list, and the abstract's stated source date range (2020-2026) contradicts the body's (2015-2026).

nodes.label: Add inline citations and reconcile the date range
nodes.detail: Adds bracketed inline citations to every body paragraph, adds a 'Src.' column to Table 1 so each trial row cites its specific study, and corrects the abstract's date range to match the body (2015-2026, reflecting the FINGER trial). Rebuilds the PDF and confirms it still fits 3 pages at exactly 250 abstract words.

nodes.label: Review the corrected PDF
nodes.detail: Reads through the updated 3-page document in Acrobat, checking the newly added inline citations, the Table 1 source column, and the corrected abstract date range.

nodes.label: Request a combined figure, conclusion, and spacing fix
nodes.detail: Lists four fixes: separate the overlapping Figure 2 legend from the bars, remove citations from the conclusion since it should read as a general summary, add spacing between the table and following text, and stack Figures 1 and 2 vertically instead of side-by-side as is typical for a paper.

nodes.label: Apply the four requested fixes
nodes.detail: Removes citations from the conclusion, redesigns both figures with a legend that sits clearly below or inside the plot area, restructures the layout to stack the two figures vertically with individual captions, and adds spacing after the table. Rebuilds and visually confirms the document still holds at 3 pages.

nodes.label: Review the updated PDF
nodes.detail: Reviews the revised document after Claude applies the requested figure, conclusion, and spacing changes.

nodes.label: Report the missing Figure 2 legend
Investigate and fix the Figure 2 legend rendering issue
Review the Figure 2 legend fix
Request a references page break and spacing cleanup
Insert the page break and restyle the reference list
nodes.detail: Adds a page break so References begin fresh on their own page, increases the font size and line spacing between entries now that the section has a full page to itself, and rebuilds and visually verifies the final 3-page layout.

nodes.label: Review the reformatted references page
Confirm completion of the paper

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source: User requests to draft the body of the paper. 
Target: Finalized paper 
Reasoning: User accpets the final output of AI  through multiple refinements within Claude without their own modification.

nodes.label: Close out the session
nodes.detail: Acknowledges the completed paper, wishes the user luck, and notes the conversation can be revisited later to expand a section or swap in new trial data.

nodes.label: Finish the session

ratings.output_quality_reason: It provided links but would not provide downloaded PDFs that it could have gotten from the Google Scholar site. It did focus on the correct topic and pull information from abstracts and text, without providing the actual articles.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: It did not supply 25 research articles. It reviewed articles and pulled content from them in a later step.

Step 2.step_action: Ask the Claude Agent to write an abstract of 250 words or less.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Abstract was the appropriate length and well-written. It summarized main points but did not at first highlight which were human studies.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: It wrote an abstract of the appropriate length. It was well-written and summarized the articles.

rubrics: Spelling, grammar, and punctuation are correct

ratings.output_quality_reason: It followed my instructions but put a footer at the end that was not appropriate for the abstract. It deleted it when I asked it to.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: It edited the abstract according to my directions. Spelling, grammar, and punctuation were correct. The abstract was well-written overall.
